tasks.title: Sec A · 第 1 组
tasks.context: Questions 1 to 4 are based on the conversation you have just heard.

questions.stem: What has the woman been thinking of doing for this summer?

options.A: Spending their holidays in a novel way
options.B: Exploring more summer holiday resorts.
options.C: Surfing online to check out the best deals.
options.D: Renting a car instead of driving their own.

questions.cn: 女士一直在考虑今年夏天做什么？

optionsCn.A: 以新颖的方式度过假期。
optionsCn.B: 探索更多夏季度假胜地。
optionsCn.C: 上网查找最划算的交易。
optionsCn.D: 租车而不是开自己的车。

questions.stem: What do we learn about the man’s grandfather from the conversation?

options.A: He did not like to be locked into one place.
options.B: He did not find holiday homes appealing.
options.C: He was well travelled.
options.D: He once owned a van.

questions.cn: 从对话中我们了解到男士的祖父什么？

optionsCn.A: 他不喜欢被拴在一个地方。
optionsCn.B: 他觉得度假房没有吸引力。
optionsCn.C: 他见多识广。
optionsCn.D: 他曾拥有过一辆房车。

questions.stem: What can many camper vans do nowadays according to the woman?

options.A: Generate their own electricity.
options.B: Drive under any weather condition.
options.C: Receive instructions via computers.
options.D: Ensure the safety of passengers.

questions.cn: 根据女士，如今许多房车能做什么？

optionsCn.A: 自行发电。
optionsCn.B: 在任何天气条件下都能行驶。
optionsCn.C: 通过电脑接收指令。
optionsCn.D: 确保乘客安全。

questions.stem: What idea does the woman find attractive?

options.A: Riding one’s mountain bike on vacation.
options.B: Slowing down in one’s increasingly hectic life.
options.C: Enjoying the freedom to choose where to go and work.
options.D: Having one’s basic needs covered while away from home.

questions.cn: 女士觉得什么主意很有吸引力？

optionsCn.A: 度假时骑山地车。
optionsCn.B: 在越来越忙乱的生活中放慢节奏。
optionsCn.C: 享受自由选择去哪、在哪工作。
optionsCn.D: 在外时基本需求都能得到满足。

lines.t: So, I’ve been thinking, this summer, instead of our usual holiday rental, I’d like to try renting a camper van and exploring a bit more.
lines.cn: 我一直在想，今年夏天，我们别像往常那样租度假房了，我想试试租一辆房车，多走走看看。

lines.t: A camper van?
lines.cn: 房车？

lines.t: You mean to spend the summer living out of a car?
lines.cn: 你是说整个夏天都住在车里？

lines.t: Yes, a camper van.
lines.cn: 对，就是房车。

lines.t: And no, it’s nothing like living out of a car.
lines.cn: 而且不，这跟住在车里完全不是一回事。

lines.t: These are proper vans with full-size beds to sleep in.
lines.cn: 那是真正的房车，里面有标准尺寸的床可以睡。

lines.t: Some even have kitchens.
lines.cn: 有些甚至带厨房。

lines.t: This way, we wouldn’t have to be locked into one place during our holiday.
lines.cn: 这样一来，假期里我们就不用被拴在一个地方。

lines.t: We’d be able to visit so many more places and travel at our own pace.
lines.cn: 我们能去更多地方，按自己的节奏旅行。

lines.t: The rates of most hotels and holiday homes really soar in the summer anyway.
lines.cn: 而且夏天大多数酒店和度假房的价钱都涨得厉害。

lines.t: We’d probably save a lot of money as well.
lines.cn: 我们大概还能省下不少钱。

lines.t: I think my grandfather had a van like that.
lines.cn: 我记得我爷爷以前就有过那样一辆车。

lines.t: It doesn’t sound that appealing to me.
lines.cn: 这听起来对我没什么吸引力。

lines.t: Today’s camper vans are completely different.
lines.cn: 如今的房车已经完全不一样了。

lines.t: These days, they’re equipped with all the modern comforts.
lines.cn: 现在它们配齐了各种现代化的舒适设施。

lines.t: I’ve seen quite a few with solar panels that provide electricity for when you’re stopped.
lines.cn: 我见过不少带太阳能板的，停车时也能供电。

lines.t: This way you can still use your computer or charge your phone.
lines.cn: 这样你还是能用电脑、给手机充电。

lines.t: And most even have Wi-Fi, so if the weather’s not great, you could stream videos.
lines.cn: 大多数甚至还有 Wi-Fi，所以天气不好的时候，你还能看视频。

lines.t: I’m warming up to the idea. Keep talking.
lines.cn: 我开始对这个主意感兴趣了。继续说。

lines.t: Loads of people are committing to this trend full time.
lines.cn: 很多人正全职投入这种生活方式。

lines.t: Check it out online.
lines.cn: 上网看看吧。

lines.t: Lots of people stream videos of their alternative lifestyles and actually earn a salary.
lines.cn: 许多人靠直播自己的另类生活方式赚到了收入。

lines.t: Imagine having that kind of freedom to go anywhere you want and work from anywhere in the world.
lines.cn: 想象一下拥有那种自由：想去哪儿就去哪儿，在世界任何地方工作。

lines.t: Okay, we can consider it.
lines.cn: 好，我们可以考虑一下。

lines.t: As long as the basic needs like toilets and showers are covered, I’m definitely in.
lines.cn: 只要像厕所和淋浴这样的基本需求能满足，我绝对加入。

lines.t: Do you think there’ll be enough room for my mountain bike?
lines.cn: 你觉得有足够空间放我的山地车吗？

lines.t: What about food delivery?
lines.cn: 外卖怎么办？

lines.t: Will we be able to order to the van?
lines.cn: 我们能点餐送到房车吗？

lines.t: Will there be enough space for the dog?
lines.cn: 有足够空间给狗吗？

lines.t: We wouldn’t want to leave him behind.
lines.cn: 我们可不想把它丢下。

lines.t: Slow down.
lines.cn: 慢点。

lines.t: Glad you’re excited about it.
lines.cn: 很高兴你这么兴奋。

lines.t: Let’s start by looking at what’s available first.
lines.cn: 我们先看看有什么可选的吧。

tasks.title: Sec A · 第 2 组
tasks.context: Questions 5 to 8 are based on the conversation you have just heard.

questions.stem: What do we learn about the woman from the man’s description?

options.A: Her physical health has deteriorated these past few weeks.
options.B: She has lagged behind most of her co-workers in output.
options.C: Her job performance has worsened over the past month.
options.D: She has missed several important appointments lately.

questions.cn: 从男士的描述中，我们了解到女士什么？

optionsCn.A: 过去几周她的身体健康恶化了。
optionsCn.B: 她的产出落后于大多数同事。
optionsCn.C: 过去一个月她的工作表现变差了。
optionsCn.D: 她最近错过了几个重要约会。

questions.stem: What does the woman say she’s experiencing at the moment?

options.A: Penalty for curtailed output.
options.B: Some problems at home.
options.C: Disturbance of her mind.
options.D: Serious health issues.

questions.cn: 女士说她眼下正在经历什么？

optionsCn.A: 因产出减少而受罚。
optionsCn.B: 家里出了一些问题。
optionsCn.C: 她心绪不宁。
optionsCn.D: 严重的健康问题。

questions.stem: What does the man say makes his job far easier?

options.A: The woman’s whole-hearted support.
options.B: The woman’s work proficiency.
options.C: His management capability.
options.D: His engaging personality.

questions.cn: 男士说什么让他的工作轻松多了？

optionsCn.A: 女士全心全意的支持。
optionsCn.B: 女士胜任工作的能力。
optionsCn.C: 他的管理能力。
optionsCn.D: 他富有感染力的性格。

questions.stem: What agreement have the speakers reached by the end of the conversation?

options.A: The man will help the woman get back to her usual self.
options.B: The man will be back at his 100% in a couple of weeks.
options.C: The woman will be off work on the next two Mondays.
options.D: The woman will resume her work in two weeks.

questions.cn: 到对话结束时，两位说话人达成了什么一致？

optionsCn.A: 男士会帮女士恢复常态。
optionsCn.B: 男士将在两周内恢复到百分之百的状态。
optionsCn.C: 女士接下来两个周一将休假。
optionsCn.D: 女士将在两周后复工。

lines.t: You wanted to see me?
lines.cn: 你找我有事？

lines.t: Yes, I’ll get straight to the point.
lines.cn: 是的，我直说吧。

lines.t: Over the past month or so, it has become apparent that your performance has dipped.
lines.cn: 过去一个月左右，很明显你的表现有所下滑。

lines.t: You’ve been late to work several times these past few weeks, which is very uncharacteristic of you.
lines.cn: 这几周你有好几次上班迟到，这很不像你。

lines.t: But what really concerns me is your curtailed output.
lines.cn: 但真正让我担心的是你产出减少了。

lines.t: Lately, you seem to be constantly one step behind.
lines.cn: 最近你似乎总是慢一步。

lines.t: What’s going on?
lines.cn: 发生什么事了？

lines.t: I’m sorry.
lines.cn: 对不起。

lines.t: I’m going through some unfortunate family issues at the moment.
lines.cn: 我眼下正遇到一些家里的不顺心事。

lines.t: It’s a personal matter, so if you don’t mind, I much prefer we don’t get into it.
lines.cn: 这是私事，如果你不介意，我更希望我们不要谈这个。

lines.t: Nevertheless, I expect it to have all blown over in another month or so.
lines.cn: 不过，我预计再过一个月左右就会过去了。

lines.t: Do you need some time off?
lines.cn: 你需要休些假吗？

lines.t: Actually, yes.
lines.cn: 其实，是的。

lines.t: Would it be possible to take the next two Mondays off?
lines.cn: 接下来两个周一能请假吗？

lines.t: I was deliberating whether I should ask for this, but now that we’re here.
lines.cn: 我一直在犹豫要不要提这个请求，但既然谈到这儿了。

lines.t: Sure thing.
lines.cn: 没问题。

lines.t: But if you needed some leave, why didn’t you ask for it earlier?
lines.cn: 但如果你需要休假，为什么没早点开口？

lines.t: I’m not sure why.
lines.cn: 我也不知道为什么。

lines.t: I guess I kind of felt bad asking for it.
lines.cn: 大概是我觉得开口请假不太好意思。

lines.t: You shouldn’t feel bad asking for leave, especially if you need it.
lines.cn: 你请假不该觉得不好意思，尤其是你确实需要的时候。

lines.t: I know.
lines.cn: 我知道。

lines.t: You are right.
lines.cn: 你说得对。

lines.t: I’m sorry.
lines.cn: 对不起。

lines.t: Look, you’ve been with us almost five years and I personally really value your proficiency at your job.
lines.cn: 你看，你在我们这儿快五年了，我个人非常看重你胜任工作的能力。

lines.t: It makes my job far easier.
lines.cn: 这让我工作轻松多了。

lines.t: In addition, I can assure you that management as a whole also holds you in high regard.
lines.cn: 此外，我可以向你保证，整个管理层也都很看重你。

lines.t: Thank you.
lines.cn: 谢谢。

lines.t: What I need is for you to be back at your 100%.
lines.cn: 我需要的是你恢复到百分之百的状态。

lines.t: Are you sure taking two Mondays off will suffice?
lines.cn: 你确定休两个周一够吗？

lines.t: It’ll be enough.
lines.cn: 够了。

lines.t: I’m sure of it.
lines.cn: 我确定。

lines.t: Okay, good.
lines.cn: 好，很好。

lines.t: So this is what we’re going to do.
lines.cn: 那我们就这么办。

lines.t: You will take those days off, and I expect that you will gradually come back to your usual self.
lines.cn: 你把那几天假休了，我希望你能逐渐回到原来的状态。

lines.t: Then, in two months’ time, we will catch up again to see how you are faring.
lines.cn: 然后两个月后，我们再聊聊，看看你情况如何。

lines.t: Sounds good.
lines.cn: 听起来不错。

lines.t: Thank you for your understanding.
lines.cn: 谢谢你的理解。

tasks.title: Sec B · 第 3 组
tasks.context: Questions 9 to 11 are based on the passage you have just heard.

questions.stem: What does research suggest about a higher level of education?

options.A: It can have an impact on our moods and emotions.
options.B: It can improve our financial status significantly.
options.C: It can help us achieve better work performance.
options.D: It can enable us to live a healthier and longer life.

questions.cn: 关于更高的教育水平，研究显示了什么？

optionsCn.A: 它会影响我们的情绪和心情。
optionsCn.B: 它能显著改善我们的财务状况。
optionsCn.C: 它能帮助我们取得更好的工作表现。
optionsCn.D: 它能让我们活得更健康、更长久。

questions.stem: What do we learn from the finding of the new research?

options.A: One’s health tends to differ before and after marriage.
options.B: The spouse’s level of education can impact one’s health.
options.C: The wealthier one’s spouse is, the healthier one becomes.
options.D: One’s health status is related to one’s social background.

questions.cn: 从新研究的发现中我们了解到什么？

optionsCn.A: 一个人的健康在婚前婚后往往不同。
optionsCn.B: 配偶的教育水平会影响一个人的健康。
optionsCn.C: 配偶越富有，一个人就越健康。
optionsCn.D: 一个人的健康状况与其社会背景有关。

questions.stem: What does the passage say about the men in the sample of the new research?

options.A: They had more education than their spouses.
options.B: They had much in common with their spouses.
options.C: They benefited a lot from their career achievements.
options.D: They showed interest in their spouse’s occupations.

questions.cn: 关于新研究样本中的男性，文章说了什么？

optionsCn.A: 他们比配偶受教育更多。
optionsCn.B: 他们与配偶有很多共同点。
optionsCn.C: 他们从自己的职业成就中获益良多。
optionsCn.D: 他们对配偶的职业表现出兴趣。

lines.t: There are many factors that impact our health.
lines.cn: 影响我们健康的因素有很多。

lines.t: These include our finances, our emotions and the way we work.
lines.cn: 包括我们的财务状况、情绪以及工作方式。

lines.t: Education is one such factor.
lines.cn: 教育就是其中一个因素。

lines.t: Research suggests that higher levels of education can lead to better health and even greater longevity.
lines.cn: 研究表明，更高的教育水平能带来更好的健康，甚至更长的寿命。

lines.t: But what about the education of your partner?
lines.cn: 但你伴侣的教育水平又如何呢？

lines.t: New research seeks to answer this question.
lines.cn: 一项新研究试图回答这个问题。

lines.t: Researchers use data from a longitudinal study.
lines.cn: 研究者使用了一项纵向研究的数据。

lines.t: The data came from surveys first administered to high school seniors in 1957.
lines.cn: 这些数据来自 1957 年首次对高中毕业班学生进行的调查。

lines.t: The surveys ended in 2011.
lines.cn: 调查于 2011 年结束。

lines.t: The team found that a person whose spouse had a higher level of education tended to report better health.
lines.cn: 研究团队发现，配偶教育水平较高的人往往报告健康状况更好。

lines.t: This remained the case when adjusting for other factors, such as participants’ own education, social background and health status before and after marriage.
lines.cn: 在调整了其他因素（如受访者自身的教育、社会背景以及婚前婚后的健康状况）之后，这一结果依然成立。

lines.t: The authors suggest that high levels of education provide shared social, intellectual, emotional and financial resources.
lines.cn: 作者认为，高教育水平提供了可供共享的社会、智力、情感和财务资源。

lines.t: These include things like higher levels of emotional intelligence, particular skills or knowledge, or more money.
lines.cn: 这些包括更高的情商、特定的技能或知识，或者更多的钱。

lines.t: The researchers concede that an individual’s own level of education is clearly important for their health, but they assert that individuals also can reap the benefits of their partner’s education.
lines.cn: 研究者承认，个人自身的教育水平显然对健康很重要，但他们也断言，个人同样能从伴侣的教育中获益。

lines.t: It is noteworthy that the effects vary by gender.
lines.cn: 值得注意的是，这种效应因性别而异。

lines.t: For women, health was more closely correlated to their spouse’s education than for men.
lines.cn: 对女性而言，健康与配偶教育水平的相关性比男性更强。

lines.t: The team suggests this may be related to the time period of the study.
lines.cn: 研究团队认为这可能与研究的时代背景有关。

lines.t: Women in this sample had lower levels of education and lower occupational achievements than the men.
lines.cn: 该样本中的女性教育水平和职业成就都低于男性。

lines.t: The researchers’ hypothesis is that this made the husband’s resources more likely to have a shared impact.
lines.cn: 研究者的假设是，这使得丈夫的资源更可能产生共享影响。

tasks.title: Sec B · 第 4 组
tasks.context: Questions 12 to 15 are based on the passage you have just heard.

questions.stem: What is said to be a key challenge for cities prone to floods?

options.A: Finding out the changing climate patterns.
options.B: Identifying the cities’ geological features.
options.C: Forecasting flood risks accurately.
options.D: Eliminating their root cause.

questions.cn: 据说什么是易发洪水城市面临的关键挑战？

optionsCn.A: 弄清不断变化的气候模式。
optionsCn.B: 识别城市的地质特征。
optionsCn.C: 准确预报洪水风险。
optionsCn.D: 消除其根本原因。

questions.stem: For what purpose does Derek Loftis collect the data of ordinary citizens during high tides?

options.A: To validate his hypothesis about the gravity of floods.
options.B: To determine the frequency of high tides causing floods.
options.C: To see the feasibility of his project on flooding.
options.D: To improve his mathematical flooding model.

questions.cn: 德里克·洛夫蒂斯在涨潮期间收集普通市民数据的目的是什么？

optionsCn.A: 验证他关于洪水严重性的假设。
optionsCn.B: 确定引发洪水的涨潮频率。
optionsCn.C: 检验他洪水项目的可行性。
optionsCn.D: 改进他的数学洪水模型。

questions.stem: What does the passage say is Derek Loftis’s mission?

options.A: To forecast rapid floods in real time.
options.B: To classify the flooding data processed.
options.C: To study the consequences of high tides on flooded areas.
options.D: To teach local citizens how to collect data of incoming floods.

questions.cn: 文章说德里克·洛夫蒂斯的使命是什么？

optionsCn.A: 实时预报快速洪水。
optionsCn.B: 对所处理的洪水数据分类。
optionsCn.C: 研究涨潮对洪水区域的后果。
optionsCn.D: 教当地市民如何收集洪水数据。

questions.stem: What did Loftis and his colleagues do to obtain data about water height and movement?

options.A: They tracked the rising tides with video-cameras.
options.B: They set up Internet-connected water-level sensors.
options.C: They used newly-developed supercomputing facilities.
options.D: They observed the direction of water flow on the spot.

questions.cn: 洛夫蒂斯和同事做了什么来获取水位与水流数据？

optionsCn.A: 他们用摄像机跟踪上涨的潮水。
optionsCn.B: 他们布设了联网水位传感器。
optionsCn.C: 他们使用了新开发的超级计算设施。
optionsCn.D: 他们现场观察水流方向。

lines.t: Climate scientists predict that many parts of the world will be increasingly prone to floods.
lines.cn: 气候科学家预测，世界许多地区将越来越容易发生洪水。

lines.t: This is a serious risk to human lives and property.
lines.cn: 这对人的生命和财产构成严重风险。

lines.t: So understanding and accurately forecasting flood risks is a key challenge for vulnerable cities around the globe.
lines.cn: 因此，理解并准确预报洪水风险，是全球脆弱城市面临的关键挑战。

lines.t: In 2017, Derek Loftis of the Virginia Institute of Marine Science started a project called Catch the King.
lines.cn: 2017 年，弗吉尼亚海洋科学研究所的德里克·洛夫蒂斯启动了一个名为“追潮者”的项目。

lines.t: It uses a smartphone app to collect the data of ordinary citizens during high tides.
lines.cn: 该项目用一款手机应用在涨潮期间收集普通市民的数据。

lines.t: He’ll use those data to validate and improve his mathematical flooding model, called TideWatch.
lines.cn: 他将用这些数据来验证并改进他那套名为 TideWatch 的数学洪水模型。

lines.t: Loftis’s mission is to know where the water goes before it goes there.
lines.cn: 洛夫蒂斯的使命是：在水到达之前就知道水会去哪里。

lines.t: But collecting necessary data and then processing that information quickly enough to make usable forecasts is anything but easy.
lines.cn: 但收集必要数据、再足够快地处理这些信息以做出可用的预报，绝非易事。

lines.t: Accurate flood forecasts require an understanding of the situation on the ground.
lines.cn: 准确的洪水预报需要了解实地情况。

lines.t: By the early 2000s, supercomputing had advanced enough that scientists could integrate weather forecasting models with such measurements.
lines.cn: 到 2000 年代初，超级计算已足够先进，科学家可以把天气预报模型与这类测量数据结合起来。

lines.t: But they still didn’t have the critically important ability to forecast fast-moving floods in real time.
lines.cn: 但他们仍然不具备实时预报快速移动洪水的这一至关重要的能力。

lines.t: So, in 2017, Loftis and colleagues set up a group of 28 Internet-connected water-level sensors throughout the flood risk community of Norfolk, Virginia.
lines.cn: 于是 2017 年，洛夫蒂斯和同事在弗吉尼亚州诺福克的洪水风险社区布设了 28 个联网水位传感器。

lines.t: The new sensors relayed rough measurements about water height and movement to a computer at the Virginia Institute.
lines.cn: 这些新传感器把水位和水流的粗略测量数据传回弗吉尼亚研究所的一台计算机。

lines.t: Along with those sensors, hundreds of local citizens take photos of rising tides and transmit them in real time to the institute.
lines.cn: 除了这些传感器，数百名当地市民拍摄涨潮照片并实时传送给研究所。

lines.t: Scientists hope that the data collected by these citizens can help sharpen the ability to forecast exactly when and where damaging floods will occur.
lines.cn: 科学家希望这些市民收集的数据能帮助提高精确预报“破坏性洪水将何时何地发生”的能力。

tasks.title: Sec C · 第 5 组
tasks.context: Questions 16 to 18 are based on the recording you have just heard.

questions.stem: What does the speaker say has become something of a ritual?

options.A: To debate the validity of current survey data.
options.B: To argue about the value of a college degree.
options.C: To account for the drastic decline in employment among men.
options.D: To compare men without college degrees with those who have.

questions.cn: 讲话者说什么几乎成了一种例行仪式？

optionsCn.A: 争论当前调查数据的有效性。
optionsCn.B: 争论大学学位的价值。
optionsCn.C: 解释男性就业的急剧下滑。
optionsCn.D: 比较没有学位的男性与有学位者。

questions.stem: What did the researchers of a recent working paper consider first?

options.A: The issue of changing job requirements.
options.B: The increase in women taking up jobs.
options.C: The impact of inflation.
options.D: The factor of wages.

questions.cn: 最近一份工作论文的研究者首先考察了什么？

optionsCn.A: 不断变化的岗位要求问题。
optionsCn.B: 女性就业的增加。
optionsCn.C: 通货膨胀的影响。
optionsCn.D: 工资这一因素。

questions.stem: What did the recent paper identify as a new potential explanation of the problem concerning men’s employment?

options.A: The sharp decline in marriage among men with no college degrees.
options.B: The wage gap between those with college degrees and those without.
options.C: More jobs requiring their holders to have a college degree nowadays.
options.D: Men’s unwillingness to accept low wages in times of growing inflation.

questions.cn: 关于男性就业问题，最近的论文提出了什么新的可能解释？

optionsCn.A: 没有大学学位的男性结婚率急剧下降。
optionsCn.B: 有学位者与无学位者之间的工资差距。
optionsCn.C: 如今有更多岗位要求任职者拥有大学学位。
optionsCn.D: 男性在通胀加剧时不愿接受低工资。

lines.t: Now, it’s become something of a ritual to debate the value of a college degree.
lines.cn: 如今，争论大学学位的价值几乎成了一种例行仪式。

lines.t: But as current population survey data show, there has been a sharp decline in employment among men without college degrees compared with those who have them.
lines.cn: 但正如当前人口调查数据显示的，没有大学学位的男性在就业上相对有学位者出现了急剧下滑。

lines.t: This decline began in the 1960s and has become more serious over time.
lines.cn: 这种下滑始于 20 世纪 60 年代，并随着时间推移变得更加严重。

lines.t: What has actually caused this decline?
lines.cn: 究竟是什么造成了下滑？

lines.t: Well, economists have been working to ascertain the roots of the decline for decades, and have come up with several theories.
lines.cn: 几十年来，经济学家一直在努力弄清其根源，并提出了若干理论。

lines.t: One popular theory is that it’s a case of too low wages for jobs that don’t require a degree.
lines.cn: 一种流行的理论是：不需要学位的岗位工资太低。

lines.t: An alternate theory is that there were more jobs not requiring a college degree in the past than now.
lines.cn: 另一种理论是：过去不需要大学学位的岗位比现在多。

lines.t: A recent working paper from the National Bureau of Economic Research reviewed those theories and put forward additional hypotheses about the causes of the problem.
lines.cn: 美国国家经济研究局最近的一份工作论文回顾了这些理论，并就问题的成因提出了新的假设。

lines.t: Let’s look at that paper now.
lines.cn: 我们现在来看看这份论文。

lines.t: First, the researchers considered the issue of wages.
lines.cn: 首先，研究者考察了工资问题。

lines.t: As the wage gap has grown between those with college degrees and those without, economists have suggested that men aren’t as interested in taking some of the less lucrative jobs.
lines.cn: 随着有大学学位者与无学位者之间的工资差距扩大，经济学家提出，男性对从事一些收入较低的岗位已不那么感兴趣。

lines.t: While the authors of the paper found truth in this explanation, they assert that low wages can’t be the only factor, as wages for men without college degrees, adjusting for inflation, haven’t changed much since the 1960s, making it hard to see why fewer men seem willing to accept those wages.
lines.cn: 论文作者发现这一解释有一定道理，但他们断言低工资不可能是唯一因素，因为没有大学学位的男性工资经通胀调整后自 20 世纪 60 年代以来变化不大，很难理解为什么愿意接受这些工资的男性反而变少了。

lines.t: This leads to the second theory that more jobs require a college degree today than in the past.
lines.cn: 这就引出第二种理论：如今比过去有更多岗位要求大学学位。

lines.t: Indeed, that theory seems valid, because in America today, two thirds of jobs are filled by workers with at least some college education.
lines.cn: 这一理论似乎确实成立，因为如今在美国，三分之二的岗位由至少受过一些大学教育的劳动者担任。

lines.t: However, the authors of the paper argue that there are other factors amplifying the problem.
lines.cn: 然而，论文作者认为还有其他因素在放大这一问题。

lines.t: They identified two new potential explanations: the first being the tremendous decline in marriage among men without college degrees since the 1960s, and the second being the increase in women participating in the workforce that was concurrent with the decline in marriage.
lines.cn: 他们提出了两个新的可能解释：一是自 1960 年代以来，没有大学学位的男性结婚率大幅下降；二是与结婚率下降同时出现的女性劳动参与率上升。

lines.t: These two changes mean that men might not have families to support, or if they do, their wives might be doing more of the providing, both of which might remove the financial incentive to work.
lines.cn: 这两项变化意味着，男性可能没有家庭要养；或者即使有，妻子可能承担了更多供养责任——两者都可能削弱其工作的经济动力。

lines.t: The authors of the paper concede that research on the subject isn’t complete, but they argue that their work supports the value of a college education.
lines.cn: 论文作者承认这一课题的研究尚不完整，但他们主张，他们的工作支持大学教育的价值。

tasks.title: Sec C · 第 6 组
tasks.context: Questions 19 to 21 are based on the recording you have just heard.

questions.stem: What has a market research team found in its latest fashion and sustainability report?

options.A: More and more people attach importance to protecting endangered animals.
options.B: An increasing number of people demand to free animals being kept in cages.
options.C: More and more people prioritize animal welfare when buying things to wear.
options.D: An increasing number of people follow the latest trend of becoming vegetarians.

questions.cn: 一个市场研究团队在其最新的时尚与可持续性报告中发现了什么？

optionsCn.A: 越来越多人重视保护濒危动物。
optionsCn.B: 越来越多人要求释放被关在笼中的动物。
optionsCn.C: 越来越多人买衣服时把动物福利放在首位。
optionsCn.D: 越来越多人追随成为素食者的最新潮流。

questions.stem: What have some world-renowned fashion designers done for some time?

options.A: Utilized a silk substitute made from mushrooms.
options.B: Refrained from using chemicals in their products.
options.C: Labelled all their products as vegan.
options.D: Avoided the use of leather and fur.

questions.cn: 一些世界知名时装设计师早已在做什么？

optionsCn.A: 使用蘑菇制成的丝绸替代品。
optionsCn.B: 在产品中避免使用化学物质。
optionsCn.C: 把所有产品都标注为纯素。
optionsCn.D: 避免使用皮革和毛皮。

questions.stem: What does the speaker say is unclear concerning vegan products?

options.A: Whether they can be regarded as ethical.
options.B: Whether they can be considered sustainable.
options.C: Whether they actually signify a substantial change.
options.D: Whether they effectively protect animals at large.

questions.cn: 关于纯素产品，讲话者说什么尚不清楚？

optionsCn.A: 它们能否被视为道德产品。
optionsCn.B: 它们能否被视为可持续。
optionsCn.C: 它们是否真的标志着实质性的改变。
optionsCn.D: 它们是否有效保护了广大动物。

lines.t: While an increasing number of people are trying to eat less meat, a market research team has found in its latest fashion and sustainability report that the trend is now spreading from kitchen to closet.
lines.cn: 在越来越多人尝试少吃肉的同时，一个市场研究团队在其最新时尚与可持续性报告中发现，这一趋势正从厨房蔓延到衣柜。

lines.t: It found animal welfare came top of a list of issues that people considered before buying clothes, with 42% saying it was important to them.
lines.cn: 报告发现，动物福利在人们买衣服前考虑的问题清单上位居首位，42% 的人表示这对他们很重要。

lines.t: The researchers of the team predicted that the next year would see a boom in animal-free shoe collections, since they heard shoppers of all ages say they would buy footwear designated as “vegan”, meaning the goods were produced without using any animal or animal part.
lines.cn: 研究团队预测，明年无动物成分的鞋类系列将大量涌现，因为他们听到各年龄段的消费者说，愿意购买标注为“纯素”的鞋类——即不使用任何动物或动物部件生产的产品。

lines.t: As well as being on trend—and with a much better ring to it than “synthetic leather”—the “vegan” label does convey an important extra distinction.
lines.cn: 除了顺应潮流——而且听起来比“合成革”好听得多——“纯素”这个标签还传达了一项重要的额外区分。

lines.t: If you label something as vegan, then the whole product needs to be animal-free.
lines.cn: 如果把某样东西标注为纯素，那么整件产品都必须是零动物成分的。

lines.t: That means checking things like the glue that holds the shoe together for example and the chemicals used for finishing them.
lines.cn: 这意味着要检查比如粘合鞋子的胶水，以及用于后处理整理的化学物质等。

lines.t: At the top end, some of the world-renowned fashion designers have avoided leather and fur for some time.
lines.cn: 在高端市场，一些世界知名时装设计师早已避开皮革和毛皮。

lines.t: In fact, some of the companies are now exploring a leather substitute and a silk replacement made from mushrooms.
lines.cn: 事实上，一些公司现在正在探索用蘑菇制成的皮革替代品和丝绸替代品。

lines.t: The Animal Free Product Society says they’ve seen a boom in products registered with the vegan trademark.
lines.cn: 无动物产品协会表示，注册纯素商标的产品出现了激增。

lines.t: In 2018, there were 119.
So far this year, it says, an unprecedented 1,956 have been registered.
lines.cn: 该协会说，而今年迄今为止，注册量达到了前所未有的 1956 件。

lines.t: New products are being added daily.
lines.cn: 新产品每天都在增加。

lines.t: There are fur coats that are “vegan”, plastic “vegan” belts and shoes made from tree bark or natural rubber labeled “vegan”.
lines.cn: 有“纯素”毛皮大衣，有塑料“纯素”腰带，还有用树皮或天然橡胶制成、标注为“纯素”的鞋子。

lines.t: These new products aren’t coming at an extra cost to consumers, though.
lines.cn: 不过，这些新产品并没有让消费者多花钱。

lines.t: Vegan boots cost the same as the leather originals.
lines.cn: 纯素靴子的价格与真皮原款相同。

lines.t: New Look, one of the first reputable store chains to use the vegan trademark, prices ballet shoes at £7.99, and a vegan laptop handbag at £29.99, comparable with its other products.
lines.cn: New Look 是最早使用纯素商标的知名连锁店之一，其芭蕾平底鞋定价 7.99 英镑，纯素笔记本电脑手提包 29.99 英镑，与其他产品价位相当。

lines.t: This signifies a change.
lines.cn: 这标志着一种变化。

lines.t: In the past, ethical products, whether they were fair trade or organic, came at a premium.
lines.cn: 过去，道德类产品——无论是公平贸易还是有机——都要溢价。

lines.t: However, it is unclear whether these new products can be considered ethical.
lines.cn: 然而，这些新产品能否被视为道德产品尚不清楚。

lines.t: The debate over durability, crop growing impacts, pollution and recyclability is a complicated one, not to mention the ethics around the working conditions for people making the products, whatever the component materials.
lines.cn: 关于耐用性、农作物种植影响、污染和可回收性的争论相当复杂，更不用说无论使用什么材料，制作这些产品的工人的工作条件所涉及的伦理问题。

lines.t: Environmental campaigners advise that the best approach is to buy less, never mind what the item is made of.
lines.cn: 环保倡导者建议，最好的做法是少买，无论东西是用什么做的。

tasks.title: Sec C · 第 7 组
tasks.context: Questions 22 to 25 are based on the recording you have just heard.

questions.stem: What is one of the facts stated by the speaker?

options.A: The belief is less prevalent that the world is going to hell.
options.B: The environmental welfare has worsened in the world.
options.C: The world has seen more violence in recent years.
options.D: The era we live in is the most peaceful in history.

questions.cn: 讲话者陈述的事实之一是哪一个？

optionsCn.A: 认为世界正走向地狱的信念没那么普遍了。
optionsCn.B: 世界的环境福祉恶化了。
optionsCn.C: 近年世界上的暴力增多了。
optionsCn.D: 我们生活的时代是历史上最和平的。

questions.stem: What do we learn about most British and French people in a 2015 survey for YouGov?

options.A: They did not wish to live in the previous century.
options.B: They were convinced by the statistics presented to them.
options.C: They believed the world was deteriorating.
options.D: They were actually not in their right mind.

questions.cn: 在 2015 年 YouGov 的一项调查中，关于大多数英国人和法国人我们了解到什么？

optionsCn.A: 他们不愿生活在过去的世纪。
optionsCn.B: 他们被呈现给他们的统计数据说服了。
optionsCn.C: 他们认为世界正在恶化。
optionsCn.D: 他们其实神志不清。

questions.stem: What does our prevailing mood of despair indicate?

options.A: Our ancestors’ influence.
options.B: Our psychological biases.
options.C: The current state of affairs.
options.D: The subjectivity of mass media.

questions.cn: 我们普遍存在的绝望情绪说明了什么？

optionsCn.A: 我们祖先的影响。
optionsCn.B: 我们的心理偏差。
optionsCn.C: 当前的实际情况。
optionsCn.D: 大众媒体的主观性。

questions.stem: What was a very good thing in our evolutionary past?

options.A: Paying attention to negative information.
options.B: Calculating dangerous risks to our survival.
options.C: Vacuuming up depressing or enraging stories.
options.D: Spreading exciting news around us far and wide.

questions.cn: 在我们的进化史上，什么曾是一件大好事？

optionsCn.A: 关注负面信息。
optionsCn.B: 估算威胁我们生存的危险。
optionsCn.C: 把令人沮丧或愤怒的故事一股脑吸进来。
optionsCn.D: 把激动人心的消息广泛传播开来。

lines.t: By the end of 2016, anyone who had been paying even passing attention to the news headlines was highly likely to conclude that everything was terrible, and that the world was going to hell.
lines.cn: 到 2016 年底，任何哪怕只是稍加留意新闻头条的人，都极可能得出这样的结论：一切都糟透了，世界正在走向地狱。

lines.t: It was easy to feel depressed by the wars in different parts of the world, the spread of deadly viruses or terror attacks.
lines.cn: 世界各地的战争、致命病毒的传播或恐怖袭击，很容易让人感到沮丧。

lines.t: Yet, 2016 was the best year in the history of humanity.
lines.cn: 然而，2016 年是人类历史上最好的一年。

lines.t: Child mortality was roughly half what it was as recently as 1990.
lines.cn: 儿童死亡率大约只有 1990 年时的一半。

lines.t: And 300,000 more people gained access to electricity each day.
lines.cn: 而且每天又有 30 万人用上了电。

lines.t: Every single measure of material and environmental welfare in America, Europe, Asia, Africa and the world as a whole has improved rather than deteriorated.
lines.cn: 在美国、欧洲、亚洲、非洲乃至全世界，物质和环境福祉的每一项指标都在改善，而不是恶化。

lines.t: We are living in history’s most peaceful era, with violence of all kinds in steep decline.
lines.cn: 我们正生活在历史上最和平的时代，各种暴力都急剧下降。

lines.t: Those are the facts.
lines.cn: 这些都是事实。

lines.t: So why aren’t we all optimists?
lines.cn: 那我们为什么不是全都乐观呢？

lines.t: In a 2015 survey for YouGov, 65% of British people and 81% of the French said they thought the world was getting worse.
lines.cn: 在 2015 年 YouGov 的一项调查中，65% 的英国人和 81% 的法国人认为世界正在变糟。

lines.t: However, according to numerous sensible statistics, these people are simply wrong.
lines.cn: 然而，根据大量可靠的统计数据，这些人只是错了。

lines.t: Nobody in their right mind should wish to have lived in a previous century.
lines.cn: 任何神志清醒的人都不会愿意生活在过去的世纪。

lines.t: Yet people do.
lines.cn: 可人们却愿意。

lines.t: Why?
lines.cn: 为什么？

lines.t: Our prevailing mood of despair is irrational.
lines.cn: 我们普遍存在的绝望情绪是不理性的。

lines.t: It says more about us than it does about how things really are.
lines.cn: 它说明的更多是我们自身，而不是事情的真实状况。

lines.t: It is best explained as the result of various psychological biases that served a purpose for our evolutionary ancestors—but now, in a media saturated era, constantly mislead us.
lines.cn: 最好的解释是：这是多种心理偏差的结果——这些偏差曾对我们的进化祖先有用，但如今在这个媒体饱和的时代，却不断误导我们。

lines.t: Once upon a time, it was of great survival value to be worried about everything that could go wrong.
lines.cn: 从前，对一切可能出错的事都忧心忡忡，曾具有极大的生存价值。

lines.t: This is what makes bad news especially compelling.
lines.cn: 这正是坏消息格外抓人的原因。

lines.t: In our evolutionary past it was a very good thing that our attention could be easily seized by negative information, since it might well indicate a dangerous risk to our own survival.
lines.cn: 在我们的进化史上，注意力容易被负面信息抓住是件大好事，因为它很可能预示着威胁我们生存的危险。

lines.t: The caveman who always assumed there was a lion behind the next rock would usually be wrong, but he’d be much more likely to survive and reproduce than one who always assumed the opposite.
lines.cn: 总以为下一块石头后面有狮子的穴居人，通常是错的，但他比总以为没有的那个人更可能活下来并繁衍后代。

lines.t: But that was all before newspapers, television and the Internet.
lines.cn: 但那都是在报纸、电视和互联网出现之前。

lines.t: In today’s hyper connected times, our addiction to bad news just leads us to vacuum up depressing or enraging stories from across the globe.
lines.cn: 在如今高度互联的时代，我们对坏消息的上瘾，只会让我们把全球各地令人沮丧或愤怒的故事一股脑吸进来。

lines.t: Whether these news stories threaten us or not, we conclude that things are much worse than they actually are.
lines.cn: 无论这些新闻是否威胁到我们，我们都会断定情况比实际糟糕得多。

lines.t: Really good news, on the other hand, can be a lot harder to spot in a newspaper because predictable daily events by definition aren’t news.
lines.cn: 另一方面，真正的好消息在报纸上反而更难被发现，因为按定义，可预测的日常事件算不上新闻。
